newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES SOAR IN CONTINUED ACTIVE BUYING.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES SOAR IN CONTINUED ACTIVE BUYING.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged on Friday in a continued upward move fuelled by liquidity as the market played down uncertainty over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition and the prospects of early elections, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed up 66 points, or 4.32 percent at a day's high of 1,595, after piercing the 1,580 resistance. Trade volume was 32.69 trillion lira, down from Thursday's 49.42 trillion.
"The upward trend which started earlier this week continued today. The effects of yesterday's negative news on early elections faded, " said Hasan Soydan from Garanti Secuirties.
The index had sunk 2.3 percent on Thursdsay on early election fears after surging 6.7 percent earlier in the week on prospects of a new allience to replace the Islamist-led coalition government.
Foreign Minister Ciller said on Thursday she would press Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, to make her prime minister in a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.
Erbakan and Ciller are expected to meet at 5 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Friday in bargaining about possible early elections to solve a government crisis over Islamist activism.

"Today's rise shows the market's strength. The market is very strong despite all negative developments and turned to upward direction," said Ahmet Kaplan, assistant General Manager of Tekstil Securities.

The 11-month-old alliance between Erbakan and pro-Western Ciller has been crumbling under pressure from the secularist establishment, which sees Erbakan's Welfare Party as the source of an Islamist revival in officially secular Turkey.
A senior MP announced his resignation from Ciller's conservative True Path Party on Friday, robbing the government of its absolute majority in parliament.
The resignation reduced the number of government MPs to 275, one less than the absolute majority needed to win any vote of confidence at the 550-member assembly.
Over the week the index surged 8.7 percent after last week's 1.7 percent drop.
Of the 243 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 159 to 45 and 39 were steady.
The IMKB Industrial gained 2.91 percent to 1,487, the IMKB Services firmed 1.46 percent to 1,524 and the IMKB Financial soared 5.86 percent to 1,770.
The insurance index was the leading gainer with 11.92 percent premium.

Top actives were largely state-owned flat steel-maker Eregli, up 1,700 lira at 19,000, Utilities Cukurova Elektrik steady at 205,000 and Aktas Elektrik down 7,500 lira at 205,000 and state oil refinery Tupras, up 1,000 lira at 64,000.
They made up 35 percent of the total turnover.
